--- PART 1/5 ---

RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "We need design new strategy." / "The parent slot 2 fitness 255.13, others up to 269.6. Need new strategy improving."
STRATEGY: Parent is a simple strategy that starts CC, counts opponent defections, retaliates with 10% forgiveness, and uses defection rate. The trace simulates the 12 population strategies and their reactions to cooperation, defection, probing, and endgame play. It proposes a new prober/TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that tests for always-cooperators and exploits them while avoiding retaliation spirals.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the optimal exploitation against a forgiving opponent like slot 9 is to defect at a rate just below their retaliation threshold."
STRATEGY: The parent is a forgiving Tit-for-Tat-style strategy that cooperates initially and retaliates after opponent defections. The trace simulates the population strategies (slots 9, 10, 11, etc.) to estimate retaliation thresholds and payoffs. It proposes changing the parent by adding periodic defection every 3rd round while the opponent has never defected, then reverting to TFT once the opponent defects.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / discarded the report / said the trace itself misread the probe — "So it seems that against almost all strategies, a single defection costs about 1 point if they retaliate, and gains 2 if they don't."
STRATEGY: The parent is a forgiving TFT-like strategy; the trace simulates a new strategy that defects once early and then every 3rd round while the opponent has never defected, switching to TFT once the opponent defects; it changes the early-game rule to cap pre-round-20 defections at one and adds periodic post-round-20 defection.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the complexity, maybe the best strategy is simply a strong TFT with occasional probing, like slot 8 but with better parameters. Slot 8 got 269.6."
STRATEGY: Parent is slot 2 (fitness 255); trace simulates slot 8-style TFT with forgiveness and deterministic probing; changes include probing every 10 rounds when opponent has never defected, forgiving early retaliations, and defecting against mostly-defecting opponents.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "This is clean. I'll output this."
STRATEGY: The parent plays a probing strategy: cooperate by default, defect on rounds where n is a multiple of 10 (n<90) if opponent has never defected, defect with 90% probability if opponent's defection rate exceeds 0.5, and otherwise use TFT-like retaliation with a forgiveness threshold (opp_d<=2). Simulated endgame behaviour at n=98, n=95, n=90, and probe schedule n=10..80. Changed: removed unused my_d variable and cleaned up the code.
